title: Google Professional Data Engineer (PDE)

exam.scoring: Pass/fail against a scaled passing score

content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the Google Professional Data Engineer exam guide (five official sections and weightings). Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A company plans to migrate a batch ETL workload from on-premises to Google Cloud and needs to minimize operational overhead while supporting scalable parallel processing for large datasets.
options: Use Cloud Dataflow to implement pipeline processing with autoscaling and managed execution.
Use Compute Engine instances with custom scripts to manually parallelize the workload.
Use App Engine Standard to run batch jobs with fixed instance limits.
Use Cloud Functions triggered by timers to process files in a single-threaded manner.
items.explanation: Cloud Dataflow is a fully managed Apache Beam service that provides autoscaling, dynamic work rebalancing, and parallel processing for batch and streaming workloads without requiring infrastructure management.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: An organization needs to design a data pipeline that can handle both real-time event streams and scheduled batch jobs with minimal code duplication across the two processing modes.
options: Implement separate custom applications for batch and streaming to optimize each independently.
Use Apache Beam as a unified model to express both batch and streaming logic in the same pipeline code.
Use Cloud Storage triggers for batch and Pub/Sub for streaming with unrelated codebases.
Use different programming languages for batch and streaming to avoid shared dependencies.
items.explanation: Apache Beam provides a single programming model that can run as batch or streaming on Cloud Dataflow, enabling code reuse and consistent semantics across both processing modes.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: A data engineering team must design a migration strategy for a complex on-premises data warehouse to Google Cloud while preserving lineage and supporting phased cutover to minimize business disruption.
options: Perform a big-bang migration over a weekend with no intermediate validation steps.
Export all data at once and import directly without documenting transformation logic.
Plan a staged migration using extract-and-load patterns with validation checkpoints before each phase.
Migrate only summary tables and discard all historical transaction-level data.
items.explanation: A phased migration approach with validated checkpoints allows teams to verify data integrity, maintain lineage tracking, and reduce risk during cutover to the cloud environment.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: When selecting storage for a data lake that will serve both analytics queries and machine learning feature engineering, what design consideration best supports cost-effective access patterns?
options: Always keep data in memory to eliminate storage access latency.
Use local disks only and replicate across all regions for durability.
Store all data in a single high-performance block storage volume regardless of access frequency.
Use Cloud Storage with lifecycle policies to transition infrequently accessed objects to nearline or coldline classes.
items.explanation: Cloud Storage lifecycle policies automatically move data between storage classes based on age and access patterns, reducing storage costs while preserving accessibility for analytics and ML workloads.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: A company needs to design a globally scalable data processing architecture that can serve low-latency queries to users across multiple regions while maintaining data consistency for analytical workloads.
options: Replicate raw data to regional Cloud Storage buckets and process regionally with Dataflow for localized analytics.
Store data only on user devices to avoid cross-region data movement.
Use a single global database with synchronous writes from every region regardless of latency.
Centralize all processing in one region and force all users to connect to that single location.
items.explanation: Distributing raw data to regional buckets and running regional processing reduces latency and cross-region egress costs while enabling parallel analytics workloads aligned with data locality.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: A data architect is designing a pipeline that ingests high-volume streaming data from IoT devices and must ensure messages are not lost even if consumers experience temporary failures.
options: Use HTTP GET requests to push messages directly to processing endpoints without buffering.
Implement at-least-once delivery using Pub/Sub with acknowledgment deadlines and message retention configured appropriately.
Use UDP to maximize throughput without any delivery guarantees.
Process messages in-memory only without persisting them to any intermediary storage.
items.explanation: Cloud Pub/Sub provides durable message storage, at-least-once delivery semantics, and configurable acknowledgment deadlines to prevent message loss during consumer failures.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: When designing a data processing system for variable workloads, which approach best balances performance and cost efficiency without manual intervention during traffic spikes?
options: Manually scale resources after observing performance degradation in production monitoring.
Provision compute resources at maximum peak capacity and keep them running continuously.
Use fully managed services like Dataflow with autoscaling to automatically adjust worker count based on backlog and processing rate.
Schedule jobs only during business hours and ignore off-peak processing requirements.
items.explanation: Autoscaling in managed services dynamically adjusts resources in response to workload changes, maintaining throughput during spikes while minimizing costs during idle periods.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: A team needs to design a solution that processes large-scale structured data for ad hoc querying and reporting while supporting complex analytical functions and high concurrency from business users.
options: Use Bigtable for wide-column storage optimized for high-frequency point lookups only.
Store data as JSON files in a single Cloud Storage bucket and parse on every query.
Store all data in Cloud SQL with read replicas for analytical queries.
Use BigQuery as a serverless data warehouse with columnar storage and automatic scaling for concurrent queries.
items.explanation: BigQuery provides serverless, scalable analytics with columnar storage, separation of compute and storage, and support for high concurrency without managing infrastructure.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: An organization is designing a data processing architecture that must comply with data residency requirements while enabling cross-team analytics across approved geographic boundaries.
options: Design region-aware pipelines that process and store data in specified regions and control cross-region data movement through access policies.
Store all sensitive data in a public bucket and rely on authentication alone.
Ignore regional constraints and process everything in a single uncontrolled environment.
Copy all data to every global region without restrictions to maximize access speed.
items.explanation: Region-aware design with controlled data movement ensures compliance with residency requirements while still enabling authorized analytics workflows across permitted boundaries.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: A company needs to design a fault-tolerant data pipeline that can recover gracefully from transient failures without reprocessing the entire dataset from the beginning.
options: Process all data in a single monolithic job with no checkpointing or state management.
Implement idempotent transformations with checkpointing in Dataflow to enable exactly-once processing semantics where supported.
Disable retries entirely to prevent duplicate processing regardless of failures.
Rely solely on manual intervention to restart failed jobs from scratch.
items.explanation: Idempotent operations combined with checkpointing allow Dataflow to resume from the last successful checkpoint, avoiding full reprocessing and supporting reliable pipeline recovery.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: When designing a hybrid data processing solution that connects on-premises systems to Google Cloud, what approach best ensures secure and reliable data transfer for large volumes?
options: Expose on-premises databases directly to the public internet without firewall restrictions.
Transfer data over unencrypted public internet using basic FTP protocols.
Use Transfer Appliance for large offline transfers or Storage Transfer Service with secure connectivity for online transfers.
Email compressed data files to cloud administrators for manual upload.
items.explanation: Transfer Appliance handles petabyte-scale offline migrations securely, while Storage Transfer Service automates online transfers with authentication, scheduling, and encryption for reliable data movement.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Designing data processing systems

items.stem: A streaming application needs to ingest events from multiple publishers with low latency while ensuring ordering within each logical partition of related events.
options: Randomly distribute messages across all subscribers to maximize throughput regardless of ordering requirements.
Buffer events for hours before processing to batch them together.
Publish all events to a single global queue without any partitioning strategy.
Use Cloud Pub/Sub with message keys to preserve ordering within each key-based partition and enable parallel consumption across keys.
items.explanation: Pub/Sub message ordering by key ensures messages with the same key are delivered in order, while different keys can be processed in parallel to balance latency and throughput.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: An organization is ingesting log files from thousands of distributed sources and needs to transform and enrich them in near real-time before loading into an analytics system.
options: Ingest logs into Pub/Sub, then process with Dataflow to apply transformations and enrichments before writing to the target sink.
Store logs locally on each source and manually download them at the end of each day.
Use Cloud Storage alone without any streaming processing component.
Write custom scripts that poll each source individually with no centralized ingestion layer.
items.explanation: Pub/Sub provides scalable ingestion of distributed events, and Dataflow can process, transform, and enrich streaming data in near real-time before loading into analytics targets.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: A data engineering team needs to process large volumes of semi-structured data from Cloud Storage using a managed Hadoop ecosystem without maintaining cluster infrastructure.
options: Deploy a permanent Hadoop cluster on Compute Engine and manage all nodes manually.
Use Dataproc in a cluster mode or workflow template to run Spark/Hadoop jobs with ephemeral clusters for cost efficiency.
Run Hadoop jobs directly on Cloud Storage without any cluster orchestration.
Use App Engine to simulate Hadoop processing for small datasets only.
items.explanation: Dataproc provides managed Hadoop and Spark clusters that can be created on-demand and terminated after jobs complete, reducing operational overhead and costs.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: When building a streaming pipeline with Cloud Dataflow, which windowing strategy is most appropriate for computing tumbling aggregates over fixed time intervals regardless of event arrival time?
options: Global windowing with no time-based boundaries.
Sliding windows that overlap continuously without fixed intervals.
Tumbling fixed-time windows that partition the data stream into non-overlapping intervals.
Session windows based solely on gaps in processing time.
items.explanation: Tumbling windows divide the unbounded stream into fixed-size, non-overlapping time intervals, making them ideal for periodic aggregates like hourly or daily counts.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: A team needs to ingest data from various SaaS applications and on-premises sources into Google Cloud with minimal coding while supporting data transformations and orchestration.
options: Manually export CSV files from each source and upload them through the console daily.
Use only raw shell scripts to transfer data without any transformation capabilities.
Write custom API connectors in multiple languages for each source and maintain them independently.
Use Cloud Data Fusion, a no-code/low-code data integration tool, to build ETL pipelines with prebuilt connectors and transformations.
items.explanation: Cloud Data Fusion provides a visual interface with prebuilt connectors and transformation operators, enabling data integration with reduced development effort and built-in pipeline management.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: An organization needs to process streaming data with late-arriving events and must ensure results are corrected when late data arrives within an acceptable time horizon.
options: Configure allowed lateness and triggers in Dataflow to emit updated results when late events arrive within the watermark bounds.
Wait indefinitely for all events before producing any results.
Process events immediately without considering event-time semantics.
Ignore late-arriving events completely and only process data that arrives on time.
items.explanation: Dataflow's event-time processing with watermarks and allowed lateness allows pipelines to handle late data and emit corrected results, balancing completeness and latency.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: A data engineer must design a batch processing job that reads terabytes of data from Cloud Storage, performs complex transformations, and writes results to BigQuery with optimal performance.
options: Process data row by row using a single-threaded script to avoid memory overhead.
Use Dataflow with appropriate worker machine types, parallelism, and optimized I/O to distribute processing across workers.
Download all data to a local workstation, process it, then upload results back to the cloud.
Process the entire dataset in memory as a single array regardless of size.
items.explanation: Dataflow distributes work across multiple workers with parallel processing, enabling efficient large-scale batch transformations while reading from Cloud Storage and writing to BigQuery.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: When choosing between batch and streaming processing for a use case, which factor most strongly indicates that streaming is preferable to scheduled batch jobs?
options: The data arrives once per month in a single archive file.
Results are only needed for quarterly compliance reports with no time sensitivity.
Business decisions require insights within seconds of event occurrence rather than hours or days later.
The processing logic never changes and can be optimized for fixed-size inputs.
items.explanation: Low-latency requirements for real-time decision making favor streaming processing over batch, which introduces delays due to accumulation and scheduled execution.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: A team is running a Dataproc Spark job and needs to optimize performance when reading large Parquet files from Cloud Storage. What configuration consideration helps avoid excessive metadata requests?
options: List files recursively by making individual API calls for each file object.
Store all files in a deeply nested directory structure with no directory partitioning.
Disable all caching and read files one byte at a time.
Use the Cloud Storage connector with consistent versioning and optimize for Hadoop-compatible file listing patterns.
items.explanation: Using the optimized Cloud Storage connector and well-partitioned directory structures reduces metadata overhead when Spark reads many files, improving overall job performance.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: An organization needs to ensure exactly-once semantics when processing streaming events from Pub/Sub through Dataflow to a BigQuery sink for critical financial data.
options: Configure Dataflow with appropriate triggers, idempotent writes, and use BigQuery's streaming inserts with exactly-once support where applicable.
Process events multiple times intentionally to guarantee delivery.
Use at-most-once processing to avoid any duplicates at all costs.
Rely on BigQuery's default append mode without any deduplication logic in the pipeline.
items.explanation: Achieving exactly-once requires idempotent processing in Dataflow, proper checkpointing, and using sinks that support exactly-once semantics such as BigQuery's exactly-once streaming inserts.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: A pipeline needs to enrich incoming streaming events with reference data that changes infrequently. What approach minimizes lookup latency without reloading static data on every element?
options: Query the reference database synchronously for each incoming event.
Cache the reference dataset as a side input in Dataflow and refresh it periodically based on pipeline triggers.
Embed a full copy of reference data as hardcoded values in the pipeline code.
Reload the entire reference table from storage for every single message processed.
items.explanation: Side inputs in Dataflow allow you to efficiently distribute static or slowly changing reference data to all workers, avoiding per-element external lookups and reducing latency.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: A data engineer is designing ingestion for a system where downstream processing must tolerate temporary spikes without dropping messages. What Pub/Sub configuration best supports backpressure handling?
options: Limit the number of messages published to zero during spikes.
Set a very small message retention period to force immediate processing.
Configure unlimited message retention and appropriate acknowledgment deadlines so consumers can pull messages at their own pace.
Disable message persistence entirely to reduce storage overhead.
items.explanation: Pub/Sub's decoupling via durable buffering with configurable retention allows publishers to continue producing while consumers process at their own rate, absorbing traffic spikes.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: When migrating a legacy batch ETL process to a streaming model, which design principle is most important to maintain data correctness across the transition?
options: Assume all events arrive in perfect order and never late.
Remove all validation checks to improve processing speed.
Convert all logic to process events independently without considering stateful aggregations.
Redesign transformations to be idempotent and account for event-time semantics rather than processing-time ordering.
items.explanation: Streaming correctness requires handling out-of-order and late-arriving events using event-time semantics and idempotent transformations to produce consistent results comparable to batch processing.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Ingesting and processing the data

items.stem: A data lake stores petabytes of raw data in Cloud Storage. Which storage class is most cost-effective for data that is accessed less than once per quarter but must remain immediately available?
options: Coldline storage class for infrequently accessed data that still requires immediate retrieval.
Nearline storage class for data accessed multiple times per day.
Standard storage class for all data regardless of access patterns.
Archive storage class for data needing immediate availability.
items.explanation: Coldline storage offers the lowest cost among immediately retrievable classes for data accessed less than once per year, with millisecond access time suitable for quarterly analytics.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: A company needs to store time-series data from millions of sensors with high write throughput and the ability to quickly retrieve recent data for dashboards, while older data is queried less frequently.
options: Use Cloud SQL with a single large table and no partitioning strategy.
Use Bigtable, which is optimized for high-volume writes and low-latency reads with row key design that supports time-series access patterns.
Use Cloud Storage as a flat file store with sequential scanning for every query.
Use Firestore in document mode for petabyte-scale time-series data.
items.explanation: Bigtable's wide-column NoSQL design supports high-throughput writes and efficient range scans by row key, making it well-suited for time-series workloads with recent-data access patterns.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: An analytics team stores structured data in BigQuery and needs to optimize query performance and cost for large tables partitioned by date. What practice is most effective?
options: Store all data in a single unpartitioned table regardless of size.
Query the entire table without filters to ensure all data is scanned.
Partition tables by a date or timestamp column and use filter clauses to prune partitions during queries.
Avoid partitioning and always use SELECT * for better performance.
items.explanation: Partitioning allows BigQuery to scan only relevant partitions when queries include filters on the partitioning column, reducing both data scanned and query costs.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: A team needs to choose between BigQuery and Bigtable for a workload that requires complex SQL joins across multiple large fact and dimension tables for reporting and ad hoc analysis.
options: Choose Bigtable for OLAP workloads requiring multi-table joins.
Use either interchangeably since both support identical SQL semantics.
Choose Bigtable because it natively supports ANSI SQL joins across normalized tables.
Choose BigQuery because it is designed for analytical SQL workloads with support for joins, aggregations, and window functions over large datasets.
items.explanation: BigQuery is a serverless data warehouse optimized for analytical queries with full SQL support, including complex joins and aggregations, while Bigtable is optimized for high-throughput key-value access.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: When designing a schema for BigQuery to minimize query costs, what clustering strategy is most appropriate for frequently filtered columns with high cardinality?
options: Cluster on columns frequently used in filter, JOIN, or GROUP BY clauses to colocate similar data.
Do not cluster any columns since clustering always increases storage costs.
Cluster randomly across all columns without analyzing query patterns.
Cluster on columns that are never used in WHERE clauses or filters.
items.explanation: Clustering sorts data based on specified columns, reducing the amount of data scanned when queries filter on those columns, improving performance and lowering costs for large tables.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: An application requires a strongly consistent relational database for transactional workloads with ACID guarantees and needs to scale horizontally across regions while maintaining low write latency.
options: Use Cloud SQL for horizontal global scaling with synchronous multi-region writes by default.
Use Cloud Spanner, which provides global strong consistency, ACID transactions, and horizontal scalability across regions.
Use BigQuery as the primary transactional database for OLTP workloads.
Use Cloud Storage with object versioning as a transactional system.
items.explanation: Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed, strongly consistent relational database that supports ACID transactions and horizontal scaling, making it suitable for mission-critical transactional workloads.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: A team needs to store structured transactional data for a small-to-medium web application with minimal operational overhead and standard SQL support.
options: Use BigQuery as the operational database for row-level updates.
Use Bigtable for complex relational transactions with foreign keys.
Use Cloud SQL, a fully managed relational database service that supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server with automated backups and patching.
Use Cloud Spanner even for low-scale single-region workloads due to cost efficiency.
items.explanation: Cloud SQL provides managed relational databases with ACID compliance, standard SQL, and low operational overhead, making it ideal for traditional OLTP applications.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: For a BigQuery external table that queries data directly in Cloud Storage, what file format typically provides the best balance of compression and query performance?
options: Raw JSON files with deeply nested unstructured objects.
Plain text logs with fixed-width unparsed fields.
Uncompressed CSV files with no columnar structure.
Columnar formats like Parquet or ORC that support predicate pushdown and efficient compression.
items.explanation: Parquet and ORC are columnar, compressed formats that enable predicate pushdown and reduce data scanned, improving query performance over external tables compared to row-based formats.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: A data architect needs to design row key patterns for Bigtable to avoid hotspotting when ingesting time-series data from many devices writing simultaneously.
options: Salt the row key by adding a hash prefix or reverse the timestamp to distribute writes across the key space.
Use sequential integers starting from zero as row keys for all writes.
Use the device ID followed by the timestamp to cluster all writes for a single device.
Use a timestamp as the leading part of the row key to concentrate all writes on a small range.
items.explanation: Salting or using a hash prefix distributes writes across multiple tablets in Bigtable, preventing hotspotting that occurs when many writes target contiguous row ranges.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.stem: When storing sensitive data in Cloud Storage, what is the most secure approach to enforce access control following the principle of least privilege?
options: Make all buckets publicly readable to simplify access for analytics tools.
Use uniform bucket-level access with IAM policies and avoid granting broad roles like roles/storage.admin to users who only need read access.
Share bucket URLs with all internal teams without authentication requirements.
Grant all users the same access level regardless of their job responsibilities.
items.explanation: IAM policies with uniform bucket-level access allow fine-grained permission control, ensuring users receive only the minimum privileges required to perform their tasks.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Storing the data

items.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
items.stem: A data analyst needs to prepare raw event data in BigQuery by cleaning, deduplicating, and creating derived fields for reporting. What approach best supports reproducibility and collaboration?
options: Perform all transformations in spreadsheet software outside the data warehouse.
Manually run ad hoc SQL queries in the console and save results locally.
Create reusable views or scheduled queries with version-controlled SQL definitions in a source repository.
Write one-off UPDATE statements without documenting the transformation logic.
items.explanation: Storing transformation logic as version-controlled SQL (views, scheduled queries, or dbt-style models) ensures reproducibility, auditability, and collaboration across the analytics team.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Preparing and using data for analysis

items.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
items.stem: An organization wants to prepare data for machine learning feature engineering and needs to process large datasets in a distributed environment with Python-based transformations.
options: Manually extract features from each record one at a time using shell scripts.
Store features only in memory without persisting them for reproducibility.
Process data on a single local machine using pandas regardless of dataset size.
Use Dataproc with PySpark to distribute feature engineering transformations across a cluster for scalability.
items.explanation: PySpark on Dataproc enables distributed processing of large datasets for feature engineering, scaling horizontally while using familiar Python syntax and libraries.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Preparing and using data for analysis

items.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
items.stem: A team needs to build and deploy machine learning models using structured data in BigQuery and wants a fully managed environment with AutoML capabilities.
options: Use BigQuery ML to train models directly in the data warehouse using SQL queries.
Build models entirely from scratch using only low-level TensorFlow code without any managed services.
Use Vertex AI to train, evaluate, and deploy models, with BigQuery as the data source for training datasets.
Export all data to local workstations and train models offline with no cloud integration.
items.explanation: BigQuery ML allows data analysts and engineers to create and train ML models using standard SQL directly in BigQuery, eliminating data movement and simplifying the modeling workflow.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Preparing and using data for analysis

items.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
items.stem: When preparing data for analysis, what data quality practice is most important to ensure trustworthy reporting and downstream model performance?
options: Assume all incoming data is correct and skip validation checks to save processing time.
Implement data validation checks, null handling, and schema enforcement as part of the ingestion and transformation pipeline.
Only validate data after reports have been distributed to stakeholders.
Remove all constraints and allow any data format to enter the system.
items.explanation: Proactive data quality checks including schema validation, completeness checks, and deduplication help catch issues early and maintain trust in analytical outputs.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Preparing and using data for analysis

items.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
items.stem: A business intelligence team wants to create interactive dashboards and reports from BigQuery data with row-level access control for different user groups.
options: Create separate copies of the entire dataset for each user group.
Export static CSV files and distribute them via email to each user group.
Use Looker to connect to BigQuery and implement row-level security policies based on user attributes and permissions.
Grant all users full access to the underlying raw tables to simplify reporting.
items.explanation: Looker integrates with BigQuery and supports robust access control including row-level and field-level security, enabling governed self-service analytics.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Preparing and using data for analysis

items.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
items.stem: An analyst needs to explore and visualize large datasets in a collaborative notebook environment with access to BigQuery and PySpark.
options: Restrict all analysis to the BigQuery console which has no Python support.
Process everything in isolated local environments with no shared compute resources.
Use only text editors to write SQL without any visualization capabilities.
Use Vertex AI Workbench notebooks to run queries against BigQuery, analyze data with Python, and share results with collaborators.
items.explanation: Vertex AI Workbench provides managed Jupyter notebooks with integrated access to Google Cloud services like BigQuery and Dataproc, enabling collaborative data exploration and analysis.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Preparing and using data for analysis

items.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
items.stem: When preparing data for reporting, a team needs to create aggregated tables that are refreshed on a schedule to improve query performance for business users.
options: Create materialized views or scheduled queries in BigQuery to precompute and store aggregated results for faster access.
Never precompute anything and rely entirely on on-demand query execution.
Duplicate all transformation logic in every report definition.
Force users to run complex aggregations on raw tables every time they access reports.
items.explanation: Materialized views and scheduled queries precompute aggregations, reducing query latency and cost for repeated analytical workloads accessed by many users.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Preparing and using data for analysis

items.stem: A data engineering team needs to orchestrate complex workflows that include Dataflow jobs, Dataproc jobs, and BigQuery loads with dependencies and retry logic.
options: Manually trigger each job in sequence through the Google Cloud console.
Use Cloud Composer, a managed Apache Airflow service, to define directed acyclic graphs with scheduling, retries, and dependencies.
Write shell scripts with hardcoded sleep commands and no failure handling.
Rely on cron jobs running on a single Compute Engine instance with no monitoring.
items.explanation: Cloud Composer provides managed Airflow orchestration for complex workflows with dependency management, scheduling, alerting, and automatic retries for data pipeline tasks.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads

items.stem: A production data pipeline is experiencing intermittent failures. What observability practice best helps the team identify root causes and detect issues proactively?
options: Only check logs once per month during scheduled maintenance windows.
Wait for users to report problems before investigating any issues.
Instrument pipelines with Cloud Logging, Cloud Monitoring, and create alerting policies on key metrics like throughput, latency, and error rates.
Disable all logging to reduce storage costs and noise.
items.explanation: Centralized logging and monitoring with proactive alerting enables early detection of anomalies and accelerates root cause analysis for production data pipelines.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads

items.stem: A team needs to implement CI/CD for data pipelines to ensure changes are tested and deployed consistently across environments.
options: Edit pipeline definitions only in production to avoid environment drift.
Share production credentials across all developers without access controls.
Deploy pipeline changes directly to production without any testing or code review.
Use version control with automated testing and Cloud Build or similar CI/CD tools to validate and deploy pipeline code through staging to production.
items.explanation: Implementing CI/CD with automated testing, linting, and staged deployments reduces errors, improves reliability, and ensures consistent pipeline behavior across environments.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads

items.stem: An organization needs to optimize BigQuery costs for a growing analytics workload. What cost management practice is most effective for long-term control?
options: Use slot reservations where appropriate, partition tables, cluster data, and set budgets with alerting policies to monitor consumption.
Scan entire multi-terabyte tables in every query to maximize resource utilization.
Disable query result caching to force recomputation on every access.
Never set any quotas or budgets and allow unlimited spending.
items.explanation: Combining partitioning, clustering, query optimization, slot management, and budget alerts helps control costs while maintaining performance as data volumes grow.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads

items.stem: A data pipeline processes sensitive information and must meet compliance requirements. What practice best supports auditability and security maintenance?
options: Disable audit logging to avoid capturing sensitive access details.
Enable Cloud Audit Logs, implement least-privilege IAM, and maintain data lineage documentation for all transformations.
Grant broad administrative access to all team members for operational convenience.
Store unencrypted credentials directly in pipeline code in version control.
items.explanation: Comprehensive audit logging, principle of least privilege, and documented data lineage support compliance requirements and enable security incident investigation.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads

items.stem: A production Dataflow job is experiencing increased latency. What performance tuning approach should be taken first to diagnose and address the bottleneck?
options: Ignore performance metrics and rewrite the entire pipeline from scratch.
Immediately scale to the maximum number of workers without analyzing the bottleneck.
Review pipeline monitoring metrics like watermarks, backlog, and worker utilization to identify whether the issue is I/O bound, CPU bound, or due to key skew.
Restart the job repeatedly until performance improves.
items.explanation: Data-driven performance tuning starts with analyzing Cloud Monitoring metrics to pinpoint bottlenecks, allowing targeted optimizations rather than arbitrary resource scaling.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads

items.stem: A team needs to automate the creation and teardown of Dataproc clusters for batch processing jobs to minimize costs while ensuring consistent configurations.
options: Manually create clusters through the console each time a job needs to run.
Never delete clusters to avoid configuration overhead.
Run a single permanent cluster 24/7 even when no jobs are scheduled.
Use Dataproc Workflow Templates or ephemeral clusters created at job start and deleted upon completion.
items.explanation: Ephemeral clusters and workflow templates automate cluster lifecycle management, ensuring consistent configurations while eliminating idle compute costs between jobs.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads

items.stem: An organization needs to ensure data pipeline reliability by implementing automated recovery mechanisms for common transient failures.
options: Configure appropriate retry policies, dead-letter queues for poison messages, and alerting for persistent failures in pipeline services.
Suppress all errors and continue processing regardless of failure conditions.
Manually fix each failure as it occurs without any automation.
Fail the entire pipeline immediately on any error with no retry attempts.
items.explanation: Automated retries with exponential backoff handle transient failures, while dead-letter queues isolate problematic records and alerting ensures visibility into persistent issues.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads

items.stem: A data engineering team wants to track changes to pipeline configurations and ensure reproducible deployments across environments with proper rollback capabilities.
options: Store pipeline configurations in local text files with no version control.
Treat infrastructure and pipeline configurations as code using tools like Cloud Build and version control, enabling tracked changes and rollbacks.
Make configuration changes directly in production without any documentation.
Use different manual configurations for each environment with no central tracking.
items.explanation: Infrastructure as Code and configuration versioning enable reproducible deployments, change tracking, and safe rollbacks when issues arise in production environments.
items.reference: Google Professional Data Engineer Exam Guide - Maintaining and automating data workloads
